column2: Knives and forks were already set out on the dining room tables.
The three office girls and the couple who'd just arrived were already in their seats.
I sat down at the table {n2} had quickly taken.
A Christmas-tree-shaped candle stood in the middle of the table.
Its small flickering flame faintly lit the profile of {n2}, who was gazing out the window.
“Beautiful.”...Smooth, like an actor.
“You're beautiful.”{r}{P}... I said it smoothly, like an actor in a foreign film...{p}or so I wished, but I could never say a line like that.{g}
I just looked at her.{g}
“What are you staring at?{r}{P}{g}
With that dazed look.{r}{p}Are you that hungry?{r}{P}”{g}
...Honestly.{g}
Mrs. Kobayashi, Kyoko, and the part-timer Midori carried the food to each table.
The guests staying here were us, the three girls, and the couple who had arrived late...
or so I thought,
but there was one more guest, one who didn't quite suit a place like this inn.
A man in a coat, sitting in the corner of the dining room as if blending into the wall.
Even at dinner he hadn't taken off his coat or hat, and on top of that he was wearing black sunglasses.
He didn't look like a skier, or even a salesman here on business.
...A yakuza.
My first impression.
“A yakuza here...?{r}{P}”
I said it aloud.
But on second thought, I couldn't imagine a yakuza coming alone to an inn.
Watching him quietly
sip his soup, I began to think that maybe he was a good-natured guy despite his looks.
Maybe he kept his sunglasses on out of plain shyness, or maybe they were prescription and he planned to go skiing in them.
In any case, once our food was brought out, I stopped caring about any of it.
“Delicious!{r}{P}”
{n2} let out a voice after one sip of the soup.
It was an Italian dish called minestrone, packed with small diced vegetables.
The piping hot soup was truly delicious and seemed to warm me from deep inside.
The dishes that followed were all satisfying in flavor and portion, and sighs of contentment could be heard from all around.
I thought again that it could run as a restaurant, not just an inn.
In fact, that yakuza-looking man and the middle-aged couple might have come just for the food.
“Does your aunt cook all this?{r}{P}”
I asked {n2} over after-dinner coffee.
“Aunt just helps, I think.{r}{p}It's my uncle who loves cooking.{r}{p}He says he wanted to be a chef since he was a kid.”
“Huh.”
“He gave it up once and became an office worker, but he couldn't let go of the dream.{r}{p}They had no children, so he quit his job and started an inn.”
“...It must be hard work.”
I was impressed.
“I'm sure it is.{r}{p}But it happens that my grandfather, my mother's father, that is...”
“Yeah.”
“Grandpa owns several mountains around here.{r}{p}They had the land from the start, so I don't think they struggled on that front much.”
“...Wow.{r}{p}So {n2}'s family is
really rich.”
I started to feel a little inferior.
“Not at all.{r}{p}Most of the land went to my uncle, the eldest son.
We're just salaried people.{r}{p}Our house is small, too.”
Good thing it wasn't a love across social classes...
Just then, the sound of an engine came from outside the window.
“He's getting away!{r}{P}”
{n2} looked up sharply and stood.
Then, for some reason, she suddenly opened the door of a nearby room and
went inside.
As I tried to go after her...
“Put this on!{r}{P}”
She came right back out and tossed me a down jacket she was holding.
“Hurry!{r}{P} He'll get away!{r}{P}”
With only one sleeve on, we dashed down the hallway.
We went around to the entrance and put on our shoes.
Outside the inn, snow and wind cut at us like blades.
Then I saw a snowmobile that had come around from the back speed off into the blizzard.
I couldn't tell who it was, but there were definitely two people on it.
“{n1}, can you drive a snowmobile?{r}{P}”
{n2} shouted.
“...No way.”
“Right.{r}{p}Then you hold on to this.”
Without giving me time to answer, she pushed a pistol into my hand and ran off.
The black lump of iron was heavier than it looked, and cold.
She wanted me to use this...?
{n2} had vanished into the blizzard.
I went down the steps and tried to peer through the white darkness, but I couldn't tell which way she'd gone.
Maybe it was better not to move blindly.
Just as I made up my mind, I heard an engine sound much like the one before.
{n2} had brought a second snowmobile.
“Come on, get on behind me.”
She had goggles on over a ski mask, and gloves, too.
I timidly held on to {n2}'s back and sat down, and we took off immediately.
“Whoa!{r}{P}”
The recoil threw my upper body backward.
The acceleration was more than I'd expected.
I hurriedly gripped the underside of the seat.
“Hold tight, I'm going fast.”
{n2} shouted.
You've got to be kidding.
Racing over the bumpy snow was like a rodeo.
The only way not to be thrown off was to hold on to {n2}'s body.
wrapped my arms around her chest and clung to her back.
Beneath the thick down jacket I felt a supple elasticity.
“Pervert!{r}{P}
Hold on a little lower!{r}{P}”
“S-sorry...
I didn't mean to.”
I hurriedly slid my hands down to her stomach.
Because of the blizzard, we couldn't see the road, or even the nose of the snowmobile, but {n2} sped up without flinching.
The snowmobile bucked over the snow like a raging bull and raced down the path through the woods.
The shocks of slamming against the seat again and again ran up my spine, and even behind {n2}, the wind hitting my bare face and hands froze them in an instant.
My ears and hands began to hurt as if they'd tear off, but soon I lost feeling in them altogether.
“You're going too fast!{r}{P}
Maybe slow down a bit...”
“Hold on tight!{r}{P}”
{n2} cried, cutting me off.
The next moment, we were flying through the air.
A dizzying weightlessness felt like it would last forever.
“Hey, could you tell us what happened already?{r}{P}”
Midori said irritably.
I glanced at Mr. Kobayashi, but he didn't seem to hear Midori's words at all.
I answered, panting.
“He's dead.
Over there, in pieces...
he's dead.”
I heard someone gulp.
“In pieces...
what does that mean?{r}{P}”
Midori asked sharply, as if she thought it was a bad joke.
“What does it mean...”
Without realizing it, my voice had gone high and shrill.
“...He's in pieces!{r}{P}
The head,
the hands,
the legs,
all cut apart and lying over there!{r}{P}”
“Noooo!{r}{P}”
One of the girls screamed and burst into tears.
It was Aki.
“...Is it that Mr. Tanaka or whatever?{r}{P}”
Midori asked in a low voice.
“Yes...
I think so.{r}{p}The color of his face was totally different, so I can't be sure, but I think it was him.”
Suddenly Midori narrowed her eyes.
“Isn't it maybe a well-made dummy?{r}{P}{p}A prank, just like that threatening letter?{r}{P}”
“You can't mistake a dummy for a person.”
I remembered the cut surface I'd seen where an arm should join the body, and shuddered.
“But special effects in movies these days are amazing, right?{r}{P}{p}It's probably something like that.”
With her pressing like that, my confidence slowly faded.
“...That was a human.
No doubt about it.
There was blood, too.”
When Mr. Kobayashi insisted, Aki cried out again.
“So that threatening letter was real after all!{r}{P}I want to go home!{r}{P}”
“Come to think of it...
I've heard of something.{r}{p}...The kamaitachi.”
Mr. Mikimoto began, licking his lips.
“The kamaitachi?{r}{P}”
I asked back.
“Yes.{r}{p}You know it, right?{r}{P}{p}In this area, since long ago, it's been known that clothes are suddenly slashed or people get hurt where there's nothing around.{r}{p}The locals
blamed a creature like a weasel carrying a sickle, and called it the kamaitachi.”
Mr. Mikimoto spoke in a low voice and looked around at us.
After a moment of silence, Mr. Kobayashi snorted.
“You're saying Mr. Tanaka was cut to pieces by this kamaitachi?{r}{P}
Ridiculous.”
{n2} chimed in too.
“Besides, isn't the kamaitachi a natural phenomenon?{r}{P}{p}I've heard a vacuum forms and cuts things.”
But Mr. Mikimoto was unfazed.
“That's one explanation offered, yes.{r}{p}But whether it's a yokai or a natural phenomenon, something like that definitely happens.”
“I've heard of cuts appearing and clothes tearing, but I can't imagine a person being torn to pieces.”
I said.
“If it's a yokai's work, anything is conceivable.{r}{p}...Don't make that face.{r}{p}I don't actually believe in yokai.{r}{p}Let's think of it as a natural phenomenon.
{r}{p}Listen to this wind.{r}{p}With wind this violent, it wouldn't be strange if a terrifying vacuum, one that rarely occurs, were formed.{r}{p}Don't you think?{r}{P}”
A wind that shatters a window and instantly tears apart a person standing by it...
Had such a wind really blown?
Mr. Kayama lay on the floor drenched in blood, and Haruko lay across him as if shielding him.
A naked woman stood in front of the two of them.
Her white bare body, jet-black hair reaching her waist, and bright red blood spattered from her face to her chest...
The eyes that glared at me as I entered were unmistakably {n2}'s.
help us...”
Haruko's hoarse voice came from the floor, but I couldn't take my eyes off {n2}.
is that you, {n2}?{r}{P}”
A gaping split opened across her bloodied face.
The voice that came from it was exactly like the voice on the phone earlier.
I crept closer.
With a hiss, her long hair flashed like a whip.
Pain shot through my chest.
Startled, I looked down and saw my skin, sweater and all, slashed in a straight line, blood seeping out.
“With her hair...?!{r}{P}”
Was this what had killed Mr. Tanaka?{r}{P}
“Watch out!{r}{P}”
Someone shouted, and I was shoved hard from behind.
“Kobayashi, what's that door?”
Mr. Kayama pointed at the door at the end of the hallway.
“That's a storeroom with cleaning supplies and such.{r}{p}A person could...hide in there, I suppose...”
Everyone froze with a start.
Mr. Mikimoto stared at me with bulging eyes.
'Did you hear that?{r}{P}'
His eyes said it.
I gulped and nodded hard.
Sweat beaded on the hand gripping the ski pole.
Mr. Kobayashi, hand on the knob, looked around at everyone.
Me, Mr. Mikimoto, Toshio, and from a little way off, Mr. Kayama...
The four of us nodded at once.
The door opened.
Inside were buckets of cleaning supplies, brooms, dustpans, and washroom items like rubber slippers.
With no light, I could only see their shadows.
“I-is anyone there?{r}{P}”
Mr. Mikimoto called into the darkness.
I let out a sigh of relief.
“See, the killer escaped through the window.{r}{p}He wouldn't run into a place with this many people...”
I had just said that when
a sudden clatter sounded and a broom came toppling toward us.
“A-aaah!{r}{P} D-don't come near!{r}{P}”
Mr. Mikimoto shut his eyes and swung the mop handle around.
“...It's a cat.”
“That's Jenny.{r}{p}So that's where she was.”
Toshio said.
“Jenny?{r}{P}”
“The cat they keep here.{r}{p}I hadn't seen her and wondered where she'd gone.{r}{p}Never thought she'd wandered in here.”
“Looking at you, kid.”
...I did my best Bogart.
“You're sexy.”
...Sweet, dangerous, 007.
“Gachoon!”
...Kei Tani impression.
“Is he a yakuza?{r}{P}”
I asked {n2}.
